translation_notes: prefixes: XSD->xsd (RDF.type is written as the 'a' shorthand, so no rdf: prefix is needed).

Context shim ontouml_shim.py stands in for arguments.ARGUMENTS, utils_graph.ontouml_ref, text_values.warn_if_text_value_is_unsupported and the module logger (none importable outside the package); identical for both representations.

Literal(dimension_value, datatype=XSD.nonNegativeInteger) on the computed width/height value is the region's one coercion_datatype case: rewritten as the language's typed-literal coercion {dimension_value}^^xsd:nonNegativeInteger (INSTRUCTIONS.md trap 1: Literal(n, dt) is not "n"^^dt when n is not already a string -- the bare-braces form goes through the same int->str conversion rdflib uses, so it is safe here). The add for that branch is inlined into the g{ } at its own branch, with an early continue, rather than falling through to the shared add() call at the bottom of the loop: same triple, same condition, same control flow, just relocated -- classified minor-restructuring rather than directly-expressible because of that relocation.

Literal(dictionary_data[key], lang=language) is NOT expressible with "..."@lang: the language tag there is a run-time parameter, and ldpy's language-literal suffix only accepts a fixed token glued to the closing quote (docs/reference/language/terms.md) -- there is no interpolated-tag form. Kept as a plain rdflib call outside any island; this is a genuine gap in the language for a dynamic language tag, not a translation shortcut.

The name/type instance triple (ontouml_graph.add((new_instance, RDF.type, instance_type))) and the shared trailing add() for the plain-literal branch (Literal(dictionary_data[key]), no datatype) both become ontouml_graph += g{ ... }; these carry no datatype coercion so they exercise plain g{ } + interpolation, not the typed-literal construction this stratum targets.

Fixture in driver.py exercises: type triple, the valid-width typed-literal branch, the invalid-height branch (LOGGER.error + skipped, no triple), the dynamic-lang name branch, a plain boolean field, a restricted field (never reaches the object branches), a list of sub-dictionaries (one dict recursed into, one non-dict skipped), and a nested dict recursion.

repair.driver: six appels de plus ; le logger et le crochet Text.value du shim deviennent, dans le pilote, des enregistreurs identiques des deux côtés (sortie standard comparée) ; language='' (défaut du dépôt, decode.py:68) ; largeur/hauteur à 0, très grand entier, True, False, flottant, flottant entier, chaîne, négatif ; valeurs fausses en littéral simple ('', False, 0, nom vide avec langue) ; Text à value non vide et vide à côté d'un value hors Text ; graphe du dépôt (liaisons ontouml et base, un triplet préalable) avec un dictionnaire sans id et un élément imbriqué sans type (KeyError des deux côtés, graphe partiel comparé).
mutants_killed: garde type(dimension_value) is not int retirée
continue retiré après l'îlot typé (déjà tué)
repair.remaining: Deux mutants restent verts et sont équivalents, non comptés : `language != ""` -> `True` (rdflib 7.2.1 rend Literal(x, lang='') identique à Literal(x)) et `{dimension_value}` -> `{str(dimension_value)}` dans l'îlot typé (la garde ne laisse passer que des int exacts, dont la forme canonique est str(n)).

optimization_notes: optimized.py: `for key, value in dictionary_data.items()` replaces `keys()` + repeated `dictionary_data[key]`. The intermediate names instance_uri, instance_type, new_predicate and dimension_value are inlined, and so is non_negative_integer_fields (`key in ("width", "height")`). The id/type skip and the restricted_fields skip are merged into one `if key in ("id", "type") or key in restricted_fields: continue`; this is safe because "value" belongs to neither, so the Text.value check that sat between them is not affected. `language != ""` becomes `language`. ontouml_ref is pure (URIRef of a constant + name), so calling it after the object branch instead of before has no effect on any input.

Error handling kept: the `"id" not in` early return, the LOGGER.error + continue on an invalid width/height (same message, `{value!r}` in place of `{dimension_value!r}`, the same value), the Text.value hook and the KeyError on a missing type.

optimized.ldpy, written from optimized.py: `@graph ontouml_graph` once, then `+{ {new_instance} a {ontouml_ref(dictionary_data["type"])} }` and the shared `+{ {new_instance} {ontouml_ref(key)} {new_object} }`. The typed branch becomes `new_object = f"{value}"^^xsd:nonNegativeInteger`: the guard admits only exact ints, and str(int) is rdflib's canonical lexical form. The translation's inlined add + continue is no longer needed.

Not compressed: `Literal(value, lang=language)` (the tag is a run-time value, no island form) and the plain `Literal(value)` branch, kept as a Python call because `f{value}` raises on None where Literal(None) gives "None". URIRef(base + id) is kept on both sides, not `f<…>`: a non-str id raises TypeError in the original, and firi would str() it silently.
No exception to the symmetry rule.
header_optimization_notes: Python: nothing unused, so optimized_header.py is a copy of optimized.py.
LD Python: RDF and XSD go from the rdflib import (the region writes `a` and xsd:). Graph, URIRef and Literal stay. The xsd @prefix is used.
